newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - firm in November.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - firm in November.

text.p: High prices and premiums in Gulf middle distillate markets should be sustained well into November because of strong Asian demand, tight supplies and refinery maintenance work in the region, Gulf traders said on Thursday.

Sustained Asian demand, particulary from Indonesia, and planned maintenance work in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait next month, should keep Gulf gas oil and jet kerosene outright prices clamped to five-year highs and sustain strong market premiums.

Both the 305,000 barrels per day (bpd) capacity Jubail refinery in Saudi Arabia and part of the 420,000 bpd Mina al-Ahmadi in Kuwait are scheduled for maintenance work in November, potentially cutting supplies, traders said.
This will be followed by work at Bahrain's 250,000 bpd capacity Sitra refinery in December, trade sources said.
Gas oil was quoted at $29.00 fob Gulf on Thursday, 75 cents up on the week, while sellers of 0.5 percent grade angled for a premium of $1.10-$1.15, 80 to 90 cents for one percent sulphur.
"Gas oil is fundamentally strong...Margins are huge," one Gulf trader said.
Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) award of 520,000 tonnes of high speed diesel for December, predominantly one percent sulphur, was within market expectations, traders said.

Kerosene fundamentals were less robust at 75 cents to 80 cents to outright prices of around $29.05 a barrel, up from $28.50 on October 24, though Aden and Bahraini material was sold into Indonesia which is still dealing with refinery problems.
Kerosene's premium grew in $1.05 in November 1995 from 70 to 80 cents the previous month as heating demand took off.
Short-term market direction would be shaped by IOC's December superior kerosene buying tender.
Gulf traders are expecting IOC to award some five cargoes, or 180,000 tonnes, of kerosene.
In Gulf term product negotiations for 1997, Saudi Arabia has been able to secure greatly improved premiums for naphtha, gas oil and kerosene from its customers, traders said.
A-180 naphtha premium from Ras Tanura has been raised to $6.50 from $3.40 and diesel to 90 cents to $1.00 from 70 cents.
